meta.title: LORE — physical product studio for creators
meta.description: LORE designs and launches physical products for creators and bloggers — fully turnkey, from idea to delivery.

hero.body: We design and launch physical products for creators and bloggers — completely turnkey.

positioning.body: We build a product that naturally extends the creator's brand — one their audience actually wants to buy.
positioning.note: (for anyone tired of logo t-shirts in commercial proposals)

regular.note: And that's if you already show up with a finished brief
regular.restNote: Everything after that is on you:

us.note: You can come to us without even a finished idea.

services.body: We take on everything. From idea to delivery. You're at the center of the brand, we're behind the curtain.

production.body: We handle the entire path of the product — from development to delivery.

quality.body: Cracked glass, a crooked label, or a dented box is a hit to your reputation, not ours. So we choose materials and print the way we would for our own brand.

items.title: Material density
items.body: We measure cardboard, glass, or fabric weight in every batch — it can't drift between deliveries.

items.title: Print registration
items.body: Layer misalignment tolerance is under 0.5 mm, whether it's a label, a cover, or a t-shirt.

items.title: Seal & durability
items.body: Bottles get checked for leaks, boxes for compression and drop resistance.

items.title: Manual assembly check
items.body: Every tenth unit in a batch gets a manual check: a warped box, a peeling label, crooked stitching.

sample.title: Free sample before the print run
sample.body: Before we commit to the full run, we make one sample on the real materials and send it to you — to check by hand, not by photo.

journey.eyebrow: From the floor to the doorstep
journey.body: The same object lives three lives: born on the production floor, comes alive in a creator's hands, and finds its person.

acts.title: Born on the floor
acts.body: Materials, samples, quality control — before it becomes a product, it passes through dozens of hands.

acts.title: Comes alive on camera
acts.body: The creator introduces the product to their audience — the moment that turns an object into a story.

acts.title: Finds its person
acts.body: The box reaches its owner — and that's the moment the whole thing was built for.

team.body: We've been at this since 2019. A founder and producer, a production technologist, and an art director carry every project from idea to shipment themselves — nothing gets handed off between departments. Runs are printed through factory partners we've worked with for years: not a one-off vendor, but a team that already knows how to make your category.

about.fineprint: Production is based out of Moscow.

items.q: How much does it cost, and when do I pay?
items.a: Depends on the model. With the percentage model, you pay nothing upfront — we fund production and launch, you earn a share of every sale. With pre-order, your audience pays before production starts. The exact percentage and terms go into the contract.

items.q: What happens if the product doesn't sell?
items.a: With pre-order, the run isn't printed until enough orders come in — you're never left holding unsold stock. In other models we work out the risk split and write it into the contract before launch.
300 units for a core line, 100 for a limited capsule drop.

items.q: How long from kickoff to first shipment?
items.a: 5 to 9 weeks, based on our recent projects. It depends on how complex the product and its production are.

items.q: Who owns the brand and the design?
items.a: You do. We put that in the contract at the very start — LORE never holds rights to a product made under your name.

items.q: How is my share calculated, and when do payouts happen?
items.a: The percentage and the payout schedule go into the contract before production starts — there's no default number, it's set per project.
Terms for defects and returns are spelled out in the contract before the run goes into production — so if something goes wrong, everyone already knows who does what.

items.q: Can I get a sample before the full run?
items.a: Yes. Before the run goes to print, you get a physical sample and sign off on it yourself — production starts only after your go-ahead.

items.q: What if I don't have a product idea?
items.a: You don't need to come with one. We look at your audience — who they are, what they care about, what they'd pay for — and suggest a product that fits your brand.

items.q: How big does my audience need to be for this to make sense?
items.a: 30,000 engaged followers, as a starting point. Past that, reach matters less than how much your audience trusts your picks.
